source.title: Can Native Safety Travel? Reusing Safety Pretraining Across Models via On-Policy Distillation
source.authors: Bing-Qi Shang; Yang Zhang; Yi-Wei Chen; Chang-Sheng Wang; Shi-Yu Chang; Bing-Quan Shen; Si-Jia Liu

page_placements.theme: Unlearning recovery and resistance depend on method

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether safety behavior survives subsequent benign or harmful fine-tuning, using safety-pretrained and post-trained models and distillation variants. It is a conceptual test of fine-tuning-related safety erosion, not a reproduction of the cited first-token KL or prefilling experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own ASR results before and after GSM8K fine-tuning, including mixtures with harmful BeaverTails data. Rows from Tables 2 and 3 record benchmark-level results and selected reported averages; Fig. 4 rows use only values stated in the text. The paper's descriptions of earlier studies are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own harmful-request ASR before and after one epoch of benign GSM8K fine-tuning (objective following Qi et al. 2024). It covers safety-post-trained, safety-pretrained and distilled 1.7B–8B models, plus a VLM after ScienceQA fine-tuning. It also reports ASR after GSM8K fine-tuning with BeaverTails harmful pairs mixed in. These are new settings bearing on V2 and V1. The paper's main aim is a mitigation (distillation), but its baseline and method rows still report how often the behaviour appears.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. On-policy distillation from a safety-pretrained teacher yields students more robust to later fine-tuning than safety post-training and more useful than the teacher. Transfer is incomplete: a gap remains across model families, and the advantage vanishes under heavily harmful fine-tuning. The abstract's figure is a +5.00 vs +11.58 average ASR increase for the 1.7B student.
record.recipe_differences: The study transfers safety-pretraining behavior through on-policy or cross-tokenizer distillation and evaluates subsequent fine-tuning. It does not reproduce the cited small-data fine-tuning study's central intervention or the cited first-token KL and prefilling measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with training type and harmful-data fraction, student model, and distillation method. The paper reports that cross-tokenizer GOLD outperforms ULD and that the advantage over SafePost converges at harmful-data fractions of 20% and above.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning distilled from a Deep Ignorance teacher keeps WMDP-Bio forgetting through GSM8K fine-tuning (31.32→31.97), whereas RMU recovers knowledge (28.07→36.25).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning recovers post-hoc-unlearned hazardous knowledge, but not pretraining-induced or distilled unlearning.

fits_no_version.finding: Fig. 3 (right): on-policy distillation and SafePre suppress harmful-word next-token probabilities on JBB completions; safety post-training has little effect. This is not a per-position depth measure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety post-training barely changes harmful-token probabilities in continuations, unlike safety pretraining.

record.code_released: Will be released upon publication; URL not stated
record.problems: The authors note that only one safety-pretrained teacher was available. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the cited ASR results. The harmful-fine-tuning experiment uses a synthetic data mixture, and the exact number of harmful examples is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 4 also plots harmful-data ratios 1%, 5%, and 30%; their exact values are not stated in the text and were not transcribed. Tables 2 and 3 report additional aggregate averages for some methods; benchmark-level results were retained, with selected aggregates included for the main comparisons. Table 5's other utility scores and Figure 5's epoch-by-epoch unlearning trajectory were not included.

untested.parts: Exact number of harmful examples (only fractions of GSM8K given); the few-to-few-hundred range; near-total removal of refusal; pure harmful fine-tuning without benign mixing.
Benign datasets other than GSM8K (and ScienceQA for the VLM); carefully selected benign data; models larger than 8B; multi-epoch effects on refusal.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding attacks.
No localization of safety to weights or ranks.
Argues post-training is shallow because of small data and budget, but runs no test of the cause of token-depth shallowness.
Safety pretraining and distillation are framed as deeper safety, but depth across response positions is never measured.

missing.what: ASR at 1%, 5%, 30% harmful ratios and SafePre at 0%/10% (plot only, declared in rows_left_out); SafePre's 0% value is needed to read F4-PRE rows.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source; Qi et al. 2024 is cited and its fine-tuning objective adopted. Judge is the HarmBench classifier with greedy decoding, not the originals' GPT-4 judge. No uncertainty estimates. One safety-pretrained teacher only. The 0% harmful-ratio Fig. 4 rows were mislinked as V1 label evidence and lack a pre-fine-tuning baseline.

versions.untested_parts: The paper varies the fraction of harmful fine-tuning data, but does not state the number of harmful examples or test the specific few-to-a-few-hundred-example range. It does not test whether refusal is removed almost entirely.
Tests GSM8K fine-tuning, not a range of ordinary instruction datasets or carefully selected benign datasets.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding interventions.
No localization of safety behavior to weights, ranks, or parameters.
Does not test whether the data or objective causes first-token shallowness.
Measures fine-tuning robustness of safety pretraining and distillation, but does not test whether safety is spread beyond the first response tokens.

relationships.condition: Safety-post-trained models and post-trained or off-policy/ULD-distilled students, 1.7B–8B, after one epoch of GSM8K; Qwen2.5-VL-3B SafePost after ScienceQA
relationships.reason: ASR rises several-fold on all four benchmarks (e.g. SafePost avg 2.58→14.16; Llama-3.2-3B SafePost 0.55→18.74; VLM 0→33.26). Rows T2-SPOST-*, T2-SPD-*, T2-SOD-*, T3-3B-SP-*, T3-3B-ULD-*, T3-8B-SP-*, VLM-POST.
relationships.display_finding: Attack success rose several-fold on all four benchmarks, for example from 2.58 to 14.16 on average for SafePost, from 0.55 to 18.74 for Llama-3.2-3B SafePost, and from 0 to 33.26 for the vision-language model.
